- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.00) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast to account for potential rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction by 1–2% of spike magnitude.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% for first 5 days.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33 within 3 days), model lags in adjusting; apply early correction to avoid prolonged overestimation.
- Model tends to overfit recent volatility; if 3–5 consecutive days show high sentiment volatility, reduce forecast variance by 10–20% to avoid overreaction.
